title: Dangling references in both directions
summary: A ledger record whose seriesRefs and provenanceRefs point at records that do not exist anywhere in the repository.

title: Baseline context tag on a post-2014 term
summary: Carries assessment baseline-context while sitting in term T1, which would smuggle an unscored record into a scored term.

title: End date precedes start date
summary: An episode whose dateEnd falls before its date, which would render as a negative-length episode on any timeline.

title: Banking record citing a macro-only dispute
summary: Cites P-92 in provenanceRefs. The reference resolves, and P-92 covers macro alone, so it cannot be the provenance for a banking record.

title: Stray non-Latin script in English prose
summary: Schema validation is perfectly happy with this record: every field is a string of the right shape. The word прогресс sits in the middle of it, and only a character sweep will say so.

title: Invisible character and a lookalike domain
summary: This summary carries a zero-width space between these two​words, which no review by eye will ever catch. The source URL below uses a Cyrillic character in the hostname.

sources.name: Lookalike of a real ministry domain

title: Scored without both cases stated
summary: Assessed as worked but carries neither caseFor nor caseAgainst, which the schema requires for any scored assessment.

title: Record whose seriesRefs holds a well-formed id of the wrong layer
summary: seriesRefs must hold a series id. This one holds P-59, which is a perfectly well-formed provenance id. It is not a typo and not a dangling reference — it points at the wrong kind of thing, and ref-resolves alone would report it as merely absent.
caseFor: Present so the record fails on the reference alone, not on a missing case.

title: Record whose seriesRefs holds an id matching no layer contract
summary: seriesRefs holds "Not A Series Id", which matches no id contract in any of the four schemas — not the series slug, not L-nnnn, not P-nn, not PR-nn. Malformed rather than misdirected.
caseFor: Present so the record fails on the reference alone, not on a missing case.

title: A scored value on a record that states no objective
summary: A trend record with no claimAtLaunch and no assessmentNote, carrying a value whose own written definition is against the objective stated at announcement. This is the shape that produced fourteen wrong scores in the live corpus.
caseFor: Both cases are present so the record is rejected for the objective, not for a missing case.
caseAgainst: Both cases are present so the record is rejected for the objective, not for a missing case.
